title: Deliver the KiCad Parts Platform
description: Build the Rust/Tauri/Leptos KiCad Parts Platform defined in docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md. Existing CSV catalogs and local CAD libraries are read-only import fixtures, PocketBase is the selected team backend, and Linux is the primary isolated AFK integration environment. Completion requires the roadmap exit criteria, deterministic backup and restore evidence, later native Windows and macOS release validation, and no unsafe mutation of active KiCad projects or libraries.

visual_review.method: Read every journey screenshot (1280x800 CSS px at DPR 1.5) after each run, critiqued it, fixed material issues, and reran until none remained. The approved look is recorded as mulch mx-793b81.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Symbol units were small thumbnails; pin names unreadable on dense multi-unit parts.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Larger cards in two columns and a modal enlarge dialog per image (Escape closes).

critique_and_fixes.issue: Footprint REF** (yellow) and fab text were low-contrast on white.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Footprints sit on KiCad's dark board colour (#001023); symbols stay on white paper.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Missing-KiCad state stacked two red preview alerts under the yellow KiCad panel.
critique_and_fixes.fix: KiCad-unavailable and unassigned preview notes are quiet (grey, not role=alert); only the KiCad panel is an alert.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Redundant text: export failure repeated the headline, unassigned repeated itself, invalid override repeated the saved path, IPN shown twice for parts without an MPN.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Removed the duplicates; MPN-less rows show the category instead.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Single-image previews had a caption repeating the heading.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Captions only when a symbol has several units.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Datasheet link could not open an external browser from the webview.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Removed until an opener plugin exists; the URL stays in All catalog fields.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Review pass 2: a rejected kicad-cli path replaced the panel and lost the typed path.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Rejected paths are not saved; an inline 'Not saved: ...' alert appears under the input, which keeps the typed text.

critique_and_fixes.issue: Review pass 2: De Morgan bodies were unlabelled and sorted first.
critique_and_fixes.fix: Each unit's De Morgan body follows its normal body, captioned 'Unit A, De Morgan (1 of 5)'.

remaining: kicad-cli SVGs include empty page area below the body (the reference field), so thumbnails carry whitespace; the enlarge dialog mitigates it (follow-up F13).
Category shows the raw table name (g-mcu).
No committed baselines or pixel diffs; screenshots depend on display scaling (follow-up F6a/b).

visual_review.journey: apps/desktop/journeys/specs/06-team-catalog.test.mjs (hidden desktop, 1280x800, axe clean on every state)
first_pass_issues_fixed: Read-only view kept the previous editor's 'Restored revision 1' notice after switching accounts; the team column now resets when the signed-in person changes.
Conflict table broke 'Yours' and '0.5%' mid-word; comparison tables now use fixed, even columns and break only between words.
Tabs still showed under the conflict because a display rule beat the hidden attribute; [hidden] now always wins.
History named the import's random administrator email; administrator accounts now show as 'an administrator'.
After a restore the success notice was scrolled out of view; the column scrolls back to the top after saving, restoring or a conflict.
A 'Saved as revision 2' notice stayed after someone else's revision 3 arrived; a revision from elsewhere now clears it.
Headings sat tight under tables, and Save was below the fold in the edit form; tables get bottom spacing and Save and Cancel stay visible in a sticky bar.
visual_review.critique_after_fixes: The approved look holds: navy header, light canvas, white panels, previews stacked on the left, fields on the right, and the window never scrolls (asserted). The team column widens to 3fr beside 2fr previews only for team parts, so CSV-only parts keep the old layout. Plain words throughout ('Someone else changed this part first', 'Save my changes on top of theirs', 'Restoring adds revision 6 ... No revision is deleted or changed'). One alert per error state; saved messages are quiet status lines. Before and after cells use the existing danger-soft and ok-soft tokens; no new colours. Remaining minor points: the sticky Save bar covers the bottom of the reason box until you scroll; the header badge shows 'connecting' without a dot for about a second after sign-in; history dates are UTC, not local time.

review_round_2.change: 45: Yours now says "not changed" (muted, italic) for a field you did not change, so the table no longer suggests your 47R would overwrite their 47.0; Tolerance shows your 0.5%. The journey asserts the rows [Value, 47R, 47.0, not changed] and [Tolerance, 1%, 1%, 0.5%] and that saving on top keeps 47.0 and adds 0.5%. 44: the results list now shows the team catalog description ("Thick film resistor, 47 ohm, 1%"), matching the header.
review_round_2.critique: Reads correctly at a glance; four even columns still fit without breaking words. Not shown in a screenshot: the new "Team catalog: sign in again" badge state (unit-tested only, it cannot be triggered from a journey without dropping the live connection).

closeReason: Edits, restores, conflicts and history delivered end to end, with live updates and checkpoint catch-up. Two high-effort reviews and three fix rounds; live race checks passed (30 concurrent edits gave 1 applied and 29 conflicts). Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 182 tests, import check, lossless pilot, 26/26 hidden journeys. title: Receive and estimate one physical reel end to end
description: Outcome: Deliver the first runnable Inventory vertical slice. From empty inventory, an authorized user receives one real reel into a named local site, previews or prints its internal carrier label, records supplier-declared quantity, adds an exact or estimated Quantity Observation, and confirms any Adjustment Stock Movement. The compact Inventory row and part side sheet show confidence and evidence. | Scope and invariants: Add the minimum Rust domain/application contracts, SQLite/PocketBase records, protected commands, Leptos/Rust-UI views, and deterministic fixtures for Recorded Owner, Custodian, Inventory Site, Storage Location, Stock Holding, Receipt Lot, physical Stock Container, Stock Movement, Quantity Observation, Quantity Confidence, and Stock State. Keep supplier/source, Recorded Owner, Custodian, and site independent even when local defaults make the normal receipt short. Enforce whole-piece nonnegative quantities and 0 <= lower_bound <= expected_quantity <= upper_bound. Receive/adjust retries are idempotent; movements are immutable; direct quantity-cell editing is not canonical. This slice excludes partner balances, Reservations, Stock Floors, and procurement allocation. | AFK verification: Rust unit and property tests cover movement arithmetic, declared versus observed quantity, bounds, split-safe identity, retry, optimistic concurrency, authorization, and invalid input. A real pinned PocketBase contract test applies migrations/rules, receives and adjusts the reel, restarts, and proves the same projection and audit history. WebdriverIO browser and native Linux Tauri journeys cover empty, receive, label preview, populated row, part sheet, estimate/reconcile, validation error, duplicate retry, permission denial, conflict, offline, and success. Retain semantic, keyboard/focus, axe-compatible accessibility, deterministic 1280x800 screenshots/diffs, logs, manifest, and agent visual-review note through the cargo xtask AFK entry point. | Acceptance: The reel is drillable from part summary to site, carrier, Receipt Lot, observation, and immutable movements without false precision. Replaying a command changes quantity once; failed/concurrent commands preserve prior state. Expected and conservative quantities are visibly distinct, unusable stock is never called available, and common receiving fits one focused flow without horizontal page scrolling or an unbounded form.

title: See one part across local and partner-held stock
description: Outcome: Show one Managed Part distributed between a labeled local Stock Container and a partner-reported aggregate balance. An authorized user can add or import the balance, see a compact local/partner distribution summary, and open a site/custodian side sheet that labels it as aggregate, dated, restricted, and evidence-backed rather than as a fictional reel. | Scope and invariants: Extend the first tracer with partner Inventory Sites/accounts, Partner Stock Balances, Use Constraints, source/as_of/confidence evidence, and the Inventory Position read model. The same organization may be supplier/source, Custodian, assembler, or another party role, but those facts remain independent. A partner balance never claims carrier ID, Receipt Lot, manufacturer lot, date code, or exact count without source evidence. Owned, local, partner-held, reserved/protected, quarantined, and in-transit facts stay separate. No universal available total is introduced; allocatable appears only with explicit demand policy. Import/manual reconciliation uses stable partner/account/part and correlation keys and preserves previous observations. | AFK verification: Rust unit/property tests cover holding compatibility, party-role independence, aggregate evidence, freshness/confidence, no fabricated traceability, idempotent/out-of-order observations, and deterministic projections. A real pinned PocketBase adapter test imports, retries, updates, and restarts while preserving source history and authorization. WebdriverIO browser/native Linux Tauri journeys cover local-only, distributed, stale, uncertain, restricted, malformed import, permission, conflict, offline, and sync-error states. Screenshots cover overview, filters, distribution cell, collapsed/expanded side sheet, Aggregate partner balance label, evidence drill-down, stale warning, and 1280x800 bounded scrolling; axe/keyboard/focus and agent visual critique are required. | Acceptance: The row summarizes local and partner-held quantities without calling the sum available; the side sheet groups by Inventory Site/Custodian. Local carrier detail remains visible while external carrier/lot fields are absent or explicitly unknown. Stale/restricted balances cannot satisfy disallowed demand. Duplicate or out-of-order imports cannot inflate quantity or erase evidence.

title: Protect local prototype coverage while reserving one build
description: Outcome: Let an authorized user protect practical local prototype coverage and reserve one production build without changing physical on-hand. The user sets Keep local as pieces or enough for N builds of an exact saved Project Revision/variant, previews per-part Stock Floors, activates them, creates a Material Reservation, and reviews allocation exceptions. | Scope and invariants: Add Material Reservations, Stock Allocations, Stock Floors, demand-specific Allocatable Quantity, exact Project Revision/variant references, attrition inputs, override reasons, and floor-deficit replenishment signals. Reservations are time-bounded named claims; floors are standing site policies. Neither creates a Stock Movement or selects a physical carrier until allocation. Newer Project Revisions may propose, never silently rewrite, active floors. Allocation uses conservative eligible quantity, excludes quarantine and incompatible owner/site/pool/traceability, subtracts other allocations, and protects non-consumable floors. An authorized emergency override records a reason and exposes replenishment deficit. | AFK verification: Rust unit/property tests cover reservation lifecycle, partial allocation/shortage, floor arithmetic, exact-revision derivation, exemptions, quarantine invalidation, concurrent allocators, override authorization, release/reallocation, and unchanged movement totals. A real pinned PocketBase test proves atomic commands, rules, retry, realtime reconciliation, restart, and competing writers. WebdriverIO browser/native Linux Tauri journeys cover direct Keep local, N-build preview/confirm, changed Project Revision review, compatible allocation, incompatible-pool exception, Local shortfall with Transfer before Purchase, emergency override, permission, conflict, offline, and sync failure. Require deterministic screenshots, semantic quantities, keyboard/focus, axe compatibility, and agent review through AFK orchestration. | Acceptance: With local 120, floor 100, and another allocation 10, unrelated demand can allocate at most 10. Reserve/release changes projections and audit history, never on-hand/custody. Preview shows revision, variant, builds, attrition, pieces, coverage, and exceptions. Quarantine is allowed and turns affected Reservations into visible shortages. Common flows use focused sheets and avoid per-carrier selection unless policy requires it.

title: Transfer and reconcile one restricted partner stock pool
description: Outcome: Prove safe use of one restricted partner stock pool by reconciling partner consumption and moving owned material between partner and local sites. The user sees why pools cannot mix, dispatches a whole or partial quantity into one in-transit position, confirms destination receipt, and reconciles the next report without double counting or invented detail. | Scope and invariants: Add effective partner use/transfer constraints, dispatch and receipt commands, In-Transit Stock, whole/partial transfer behavior, reconciliation exceptions, and source-versus-inventory authority transition. Public supplier stock and unreceived Procurement commitments are never Inventory; once supply becomes owned Inventory it stops counting as inbound. A holding has one current custody/site position. Dispatch removes endpoint allocatability; receipt establishes destination custody; retry conserves whole pieces. Partial physical transfers create separately traceable children when identity is known; aggregate balances reduce without invented lots. Build-only, non-transferable, customer-specific, non-mixable, stale, quarantined, or low-confidence pools fail with a specific reason. | AFK verification: Rust unit/property tests cover balanced transfer legs, retry, partial split provenance, owner/custodian transitions, pool non-mixing, stale/malformed/out-of-order observations, missing receipt, quarantine in transit, and Procurement/Inventory double-count prevention. A real pinned PocketBase partner-adapter test imports, dispatches, restarts mid-transfer, receives locally, reconciles use/new balance, retries every command, and proves evidence history/authorization. WebdriverIO browser/native Linux Tauri journeys cover restricted explanation, whole/partial move, in-transit row, receipt, stale balance, variance, retry/conflict, permission, revoked credential, offline, and sync error. Screenshots show before/during/after, non-mixable exception, partial child, stale evidence, and reconciliation at 1280x800 with semantic conservation, focus/keyboard, accessibility, and agent review. | Acceptance: Stock is counted once and cannot simultaneously appear as inbound, partner-held, in transit, and local. Incompatible/non-transferable pools cannot silently combine; UI names policy and next action. Reconciliation preserves source/as_of/confidence and prior evidence without invented carrier, lot, date code, or legal ownership. Whole moves use one confirmation; partial moves request quantity and preserve traceability. Received stock remains subject to state, constraints, Reservations, and Floors.

title: Re-validate the Docker lab and document it when Docker work resumes
description:
Docker work is deferred while development and validation run natively on Windows (decided 2026-10-08). Before relying on the Docker lab again:
- Run the full `cargo xtask test-afk` with Docker running. It last passed on 2026-07-23, before the structural guard rewrite and the evidence-failure state fix.
- Confirm the offline-verified Tauri native package contract in a real image build. It is currently checked only statically, by validate_test_runner_dockerfile.
- Write the Docker-first README section, which was review finding docker_first_readme on kicad-parts-0f6d.
- Decide whether the test-runner image should include KiCad 10 for kicad-cli tests. The no-KiCad rule was removed on 2026-10-08; to add it, pin KiCad in infra/versions.lock and add it to the test-runner contract in tooling/afk/src/dockerfile.rs.

title: Resolve symbol and footprint references through KiCad library tables
description:
Follow-up from the a553 review (finding F1). crates/kicad-integration/src/resolver.rs resolves LIB:NAME by looking in the repo's symbols/ and footprints/ first, then KiCad's bundled share folder. It ignores sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table and KICAD10_* path variables.

Failure scenario: a nickname that differs from its file name, such as an fp-lib-table entry mapping g-sot to g-SOT.pretty, or a user's global table remapping Device, gives a preview KiCad would not place.

Bring resolution in line with the LibraryResolver boundary (mx-fe6936) and the provider/aggregate model on main (library-providers.yaml, provider-lib-table fragments). Keep exact-case matching for whatever file a table entry points at.

title: Make kicad-cli preview exports single-flight, bounded and self-cleaning
description:
Follow-up from the a553 review (findings F2 and F3), in crates/kicad-integration/src/preview.rs.
- Clicking quickly through parts that share a symbol runs duplicate exports for the same cache key, and N clicks can start up to 2N kicad-cli processes. Stale requests are never cancelled.
- Staging folders left by a crash (staging/<pid>-<n>) are never swept.
- The cache is never evicted across KiCad versions or library edits.
- On Windows the cache shares %LOCALAPPDATA%\org.kicadparts.desktop with WebView2's EBWebView.

Add per-key single-flight, a small concurrency limit, cancellation of superseded requests, a startup sweep of staging folders, and an eviction policy.

visual_review.journey: apps/desktop/journeys/specs/07-team-preview-revision.test.mjs (hidden desktop, 1280x800, axe clean on every state); all 29 journeys pass
first_pass_issues_fixed: 52: the fallback note showed the raw network error (a URL and an OS error code). The URL overflowed the preview column, which then scrolled sideways, and the symbol drawing shrank to a sliver. Notes now give a short reason ('because the team server could not be reached'), break long words, and the journey asserts the column does not scroll sideways.
52: the screenshot was taken while the footprint was still exporting; the journey now waits for both previews and checks both notes.
51: the provenance line left 'now' alone on a second line; each part of the line now stays whole, so it wraps only between parts.
visual_review.critique_after_fixes: The approved look holds: navy header, light canvas, white panels, previews stacked on the left, fields on the right, and the window does not scroll. 50 (signed out) draws the changed local copy: a circle round R_US and the 0603 pads. 51 (signed in) draws the stored revision with no circle, and the provenance says 'team catalog, revision 1', which matches 'g-pas:R_US, revision 1' in the column on the right. Hovering shows 'Stored bytes with SHA-256 ...'. 52 (team server stopped, cache cleared) draws the local library and, above it, a quiet warn-soft note (existing tokens, no new colours, not an alert): 'Revision 1 of g-pas:R_US could not be fetched because the team server could not be reached. This drawing is from your local library, which differs from that revision.' Remaining minor points: with both notes shown, the drawings in 52 are small but readable and can still be enlarged; the signed-out 'Sign in to see this symbol' state is covered by tests only, because the UI asks for team previews only while signed in.

closeReason: Preview exports are shared per entry (single-flight that a replaced request can no longer break), limited to 2 kicad-cli processes, and drop waiting work for older selections. Staging folders left by crashes are swept at startup. Eviction removes old KiCad versions, themes and layouts, and libraries unused for 14 days, through a trash folder so a partial delete is never served. The cache moved to %LOCALAPPDATA%\org.kicadparts.desktop-cache, apart from WebView2's data. Reviewed with fixes; stress-tested 320/320 by the implementer and 5 more runs by the orchestrator. Verified: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 231 tests, import check, pilot, 29/29 hidden journeys. Follow-up: kicad-parts-22cc.

title: Make journey screenshots DPI-stable and add reviewed visual baselines
description:
Follow-up from the a553 review (finding F6 a/b).
- Screenshots depend on display scaling: at 150% they come out 1920x1200 instead of 1280x800, so they aren't comparable across machines.
- No baselines are committed, so nothing is pixel-diffed, which mx-683e0a expects.
- axe marks 504-516 color-contrast nodes as incomplete in states 01, 10 and 20, so 'zero violations' doesn't prove contrast.

Pin the device scale factor for journeys, commit reviewed baselines with a diff threshold and retained diff images, and resolve the incomplete contrast checks. Keep the approved design (mx-793b81).

visual_review.journey: all 29 journeys, hidden desktop, --display-scale=1 on a 150%-scaled display: devicePixelRatio 1 and every screenshot 1280x800; two runs in a row pass with 0 different pixels on all 29 baselines
visual_review.screenshots: apps/desktop/journeys/baselines/*.png (29 states: 01-13, 20, 21, 30, 40-52); every one was looked at before it was committed
first_pass_issues_fixed: Screenshots were 1920x1200 at 150% display scaling; the app now fixes WebView2's scale with --display-scale=1.
10-12, 20, 21: random temporary folder names changed every run; journey folders now have fixed, readable names (kicad-parts-journeys/02-no-kicad).
40, 41: the team server address holds a changing port; it is hatched out for the screenshot. 45-48: save times change every run; they are now <time> elements and hatched out.
48: the baseline caught the results list still showing the old description after the restore while the header showed the restored one; the journey now waits for the list to catch up.
49: some runs caught the badge still connecting (white) instead of live (green); the journey now waits for live updates. 51 and 52 wait for their badge states too.
visual_review.critique_after_fixes: The approved look (mx-793b81) holds on all 29 states: navy header, light canvas, white panels with 8px radius, results on the left, previews stacked left of the fields, the window never scrolls, symbols on light paper and footprints on the dark board, one alert per error state. The hatching for hidden text is a thin grey diagonal pattern that keeps the real layout and reads clearly as 'hidden', not as content. No app styles were changed. Minor, not material: in 02, 03 and 13 the first STM32 unit draws small because kicad-cli's SVG includes the far-away reference text; 06 shows this machine's repository path in the footprint error; 52's drawings are small under two notes (as reviewed on c465).
visual_review.contrast: axe left 19 colour contrast checks incomplete (01, 10, 20, 21, 30, 40, 41, 47): rows cut off by a scrolled list (elmPartiallyObscured) and text under the open team menu (bgOverlap). Each is now checked again scrolled into view and with the covering elements made invisible; all 19 pass. A real contrast problem now fails the journey, including on a partly hidden row (checked by a temporary low-contrast edit).

closeReason: Journey screenshots are 1280x800 at any display scaling. The journey-only --display-scale (0.5–4) and --software-rendering options fix the scale and stop GPU-to-software drift and partial redraws. 29 reviewed approved screenshots are compared strictly (threshold 0.02, edges counted, at most 4 pixels); a live test proves one-character and colour changes fail. Images of the differences are kept, and updates are accepted only when every journey passed. All 19 incomplete contrast checks are checked again in view and pass, and a check that stays incomplete fails. Reviewed with fixes. Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 234 tests, import check, pilot, and two more hidden runs at 30/30. Follow-ups: kicad-parts-4a88, kicad-parts-2127.

title: Fix catalog entries whose previews fail
Desktop polish: settings UX, SVG cropping, build output, catalog root, links
description:
Small follow-ups from the a553 review:
- F8: apps/desktop/build.rs writes a placeholder into ../desktop-ui/dist (the source tree) instead of OUT_DIR, so a stale placeholder can ship.
- F9: the default catalog root is the compile-time CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, so the developer's path is baked into binaries.
- F13: kicad-cli SVGs keep empty space below the body, which makes large multi-unit symbols hard to read. Crop the viewBox to the content.
- Settings UX:
  - the 'Not saved' message stays until the next action;
  - there's no 'clear saved path' button;
  - link the alert to the input with aria-invalid and aria-describedby;
  - avoid a fixed settings.json.tmp name across app instances.
- Open datasheet links in the system browser (an opener plugin with a narrow capability).

Keep the approved design (mx-793b81).

title: Persist the collaboration replica checkpoint and detect a dropped last event
description: Follow-up from the b355 review. crates/collaboration/src/replica.rs keeps its checkpoint in memory only, so a restart re-reads from zero. A realtime event dropped as the last one before a quiet period isn't noticed until the next event or a reconnect. Persist the checkpoint in the desktop replica's SQLite, keeping SQLite roles separate (mx-95dadd), and add a periodic or idle catch-up probe. This fits the catalog replica work in kicad-parts-fef6 and kicad-parts-2254.

title: Harden the PocketBase collaboration server
description:
Follow-ups from the b355 review:
- Superusers can still write collab_records and collab_changes directly, because null rules don't stop them. An admin edit then leaves a gap in the change log, and every replica fails permanently with 'the change log skips'. Add a hook that blocks direct writes and only allows the protected command route.
- Correlation IDs are global, so another user can tell whether an ID was used (they get correlation_reused). Scope them per user.
- Document that pocketbase superuser upsert takes the per-run superuser password on its command line. Other processes run by the same user can see it while it runs, and the PocketBase CLI offers no stdin option.

title: Support TLS in the collaboration REST and realtime clients
description: Follow-up from b355. The REST client (ureq 2, built without TLS) and the realtime SSE client (a raw HTTP/1.1 socket) only speak plain HTTP to a loopback test server. Add HTTPS for a deployed PocketBase, with certificate validation, and keep the ability to disconnect on demand for the reconciliation tests.

title: Generalise the collaboration contract beyond the provisional collab_* schema
description: Follow-up from b355. crates/collaboration hardcodes the collab_changes collection and title/content fields in ChangeEntry. When the canonical catalog adopts the protected-command, change-log and checkpoint mechanics (kicad-parts-2254), generalise the contract. When PocketBase file storage moves to S3, prove restore of those S3-backed files: mx-413e14 notes pb_data backups exclude them. b355's 'independent copies' bucket is only a demonstration.

title: Keep the zero-loss report working after re-imports
description:
Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. The zero-loss report only holds after a first import:
- Unchanged parts keep the source of the older file, so a later import of a changed file fails with 'Source names another version'.
- After a supplier-only change (nothing_changed), the report shows the old LCSC value as stored.
- The main-manufacturer-part check matches stale incomplete-main-manufacturer-part problems (tooling/catalog-import/src/zero_loss.rs:397-407), so filling in a blank MPN reports a false loss.
- A nothing_changed run records no file hashes, because its audit entry has no sources.
- Inserting, reordering or removing CSV rows breaks the match by row number, and removed IPNs produce no import problem.
Needed before the full-catalog import (kicad-parts-357b).
closeReason: Re-imports stay lossless. Each import run records exactly what it read (files, hashes, header, rows, the commit and the import problems it found), and the report rebuilds the CSV from the latest run, matches rows by IPN and checks symbols against the current library files. All five listed problems are fixed, plus the reviewers' symbol, earlier-problem, row-count and file-hash cases. Two high-effort reviews with three fix rounds. Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 194 tests, import check, lossless pilot, 26/26 hidden journeys. Follow-ups: kicad-parts-7348, kicad-parts-d838.

title: Make catalog revisions immutable in the store
description: Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. Members cannot write catalog collections, but superusers can still PATCH or DELETE revisions, Changes, audit entries, sources and IPNs, because no hook blocks it. The tests rely on this: tooling/catalog-import/tests/pocketbase_import.rs:500-542 relabel a Change's kind and overwrite a revision's source to simulate edits. Add hooks that refuse updates and deletes on revisions, blobs, Changes, audit entries and parts' IPNs. Replace those test PATCHes with the real edit and restore routes from kicad-parts-2254.
closeReason: Delivered in seed/kicad-parts-2254 and verified. Superusers get 403 when they try to PATCH, DELETE or create Catalog records through the record and batch APIs. Server code cannot update or delete them, except moving a part's current revision to the next one. The collection API refuses deletes, renames and any change to an existing field's definition. Test PATCHes were replaced with the real edit and restore routes.

title: Make CSV imports check the current revision they expect
description: Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. mx-88ce27 says commands carry the current revision they expect, but CSV imports compare each part only with its stored current revision. An import from an older checkout therefore adds revisions that undo newer imported details. Send the expected current revisions with each import, or refuse a new revision when the source commit is older than the current revision's.
closeReason: CSV imports send the current revision they expect for every part and the import run they checked against, and get a 409 if either moved. The importer refuses files from a commit the latest import does not include, and imports that would undo recorded uncommitted changes, unless the override is set; the override is recorded on the audit entry. Git missing, not a repository, and side-branch cases have plain messages. Reviewed and verified with 9496.

title: Decide how CAD item revisions are numbered when content returns to an earlier version
description: Open decision from the fef6 re-review. CAD item revision IDs come from their content (infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_csv_imports.pb.js), so a footprint changing A to B to A reuses revision 1. The glossary says every change, including restoring, adds a new revision, and that the current revision is the newest. Option 1, recommended because it is simpler for people: number CAD item revisions like parts, so going back to A adds revision 3 while the bytes stay stored once. Option 2: keep content-based revisions and add a CAD-item exception to docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md. The user merged fef6 with option 2 behaviour and has not decided yet.
closeReason: User chose option 1 on 2026-10-10: number CAD item revisions like parts, with bytes stored once and the current revision always the newest. Implementation: kicad-parts-54d5. KiCad check: database libraries refer to Library:Name with no revision, so KiCad uses whatever the library file holds, and KiCad Integration must write each CAD item current revision.

title: Prepare the import route and CSV columns for the full catalog
description:
Follow-ups from the fef6 reviews, needed before kicad-parts-357b:
- The route hashes blobs in JavaScript at about 3–5 s per MiB, plus base64 overhead. PocketBase's request-body limit will cap single-request imports of real 3D models (not verified).
- An empty 3D-model file fails the whole import with 400 instead of becoming an import problem.
- Other categories have extra MPN columns (rfm 'MPN2', rvr 'MPN TBC') that would fall into part details instead of becoming manufacturer parts.
- Excluded from BOM is never set; the ART category notes say 'does not appear in BOM'.
closeReason: Import ready for the full catalog. UTF-8 blobs are hashed with PocketBase's own SHA-256: all 13 real 3D models import in under 0.7 s, down from 14.4 s, with an explicit 32 MiB limit checked by both the client and the route. An empty 3D model is an import problem. Extra MPN columns (MPN2, MPN TBC, and any unrouted MPN header) are import problems. Excluded from BOM is set only from KiCad's own symbol and footprint flags; disagreeing footprint choices are an import problem. Column routing covers all 21 CSV files, and every file pilots losslessly. Reviewed with fixes. Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 208 tests, import check, lossless pilot, 26/26 hidden journeys. Open user questions: is MS128-10F a Würth part, and should ART-0001-0006 be Excluded from BOM? Follow-ups: kicad-parts-ccc0, kicad-parts-e4bd.

title: Rename the older legacy-* crates and fixtures to the plain-language terms
description: fef6 renamed its own code to the plain-language glossary, but older code keeps the old words: crates/legacy-catalog (used by the desktop), the legacy-import-fixture oracle (tooling/import-fixture), fixtures/import/legacy-catalog, and the oracle's 'diagnostics'. Rename them to the glossary terms, for example 'CSV catalog' and 'import problem', so code and conversation use the same words. Keep the oracle's byte and semantic checks unchanged.
closeReason: Renamed to the plain-language terms: crates/legacy-catalog became crates/csv-catalog (CsvCatalog); the legacy-import-fixture oracle became tooling/csv-catalog-fixture (check command 'cargo run -p csv-catalog-fixture -- check .'); fixtures/import/legacy-catalog became fixtures/import/csv-catalog; diagnostics became import_problems. The manifest change is the key name only: all 262 hashes are identical, verified independently by the reviewer. Tamper tests still fail. Reviewed: ready to merge. Verified: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 234 tests, fixture check, pilot, 30/30 hidden journeys with 0 pixel differences. Follow-up: kicad-parts-fb66.

title: Let part edits add new CAD item revisions
description: Split from kicad-parts-2254 criterion 2, which asks for any needed CAD item revisions. Today an edit can bind Symbol and Footprint only to CAD item revisions the Catalog already has, and naming an unknown one gets 400. Allowing an edit to upload a new CAD item or CAD item revision depends on how CAD item revisions are numbered, which is the user decision in kicad-parts-9e05.

title: Draw team-catalog previews from the exact CAD item revision
description: From the 2254 review. preview_field in crates/catalog-browser draws team parts from the local library file, not from the stored CAD item revision the part uses. If the local file changes, the screen says 'g-pas:R_US, revision 1' next to a drawing of different bytes. Render from the stored blob, or warn when the hashes differ.
closeReason: Team parts draw from the exact stored bytes of the CAD item revision on screen. The bytes are checked against their SHA-256, and the revision record against its snapshot hash, CAD item, kind and format. They are cached by that hash, so a changed local library no longer changes the drawing. When signed out, the preview says so. When the revision can't be fetched or checked, the local drawing shows a plain note saying whether it differs. New hidden journey 07 with screenshots 50–52. Reviewed and verified with c465.

title: Make the desktop's catch-up at sign-in fetch only what it needs
description: From the 2254 review. crates/catalog/src/replica.rs:97 fetches every revision snapshot of every Change at sign-in, with one request per Change, although it only needs the current revisions from the checkpoint. This will be slow at full-catalog size (kicad-parts-357b). Fetch the current revisions in pages, then follow new Changes from the checkpoint.

title: Keep local-team-server --desktop data safe after a hard kill
description: From the 2254 re-review. With --desktop, the app's data folder sits inside the run folder, but the app runs outside the kill-on-close job. If the command is killed hard, the app keeps running and the next start sweeps its folder. A run can also, very briefly, sweep another run's folder between creating and locking it. The real Ctrl+C, Break and console-close cleanup paths are not tested end to end.

title: Test the desktop's reconnect and two desktops side by side; show local times
description: From 2254. The live-update journey uses a plain API client as the second person. The desktop's own reconnect loop and two desktop sessions converging are not exercised end to end; the 'sign in again' badge is unit-tested only. History and conflict times show in UTC; show them in local time.

title: Refuse imports from uncommitted changes unless overridden
description: User decision, 2026-10-10: commit first. Today imports from a git checkout with uncommitted changes (+dirty) are allowed and recorded, and later imports are refused if they would undo those changes unless the change was committed (mx-64c42a). Replace this with one simple rule: an import into the team catalog from a checkout with uncommitted changes is refused, with a plain message to commit first, unless an explicit override is given. Record the override on the import run audit entry, like allowed_older_checkout. Keep the older-checkout check for clean commits.

title: Notice changes to a parent symbol that others extend
description: From the 9496/23d9 re-review. The zero-loss report compares each symbol's blob with its top-level span, and the importer records symbol-extends-parent for symbols that use 'extends'. A change to the parent symbol would not be noticed. No repository library uses 'extends' today, so check this before the full-catalog import (kicad-parts-357b) or when such libraries appear.

title: Decide how Excluded from BOM changes after an edit
description: From the e4ee review. Excluded from BOM is set at import only from KiCad own flags: a local symbol with (in_bom no), or every footprint choice marked exclude_from_bom. The edit route copies the setting even when an edit rebinds Symbol or Footprint, and nobody can set it by hand (mx-9a51aa). Options: recalculate it from the newly bound CAD on every edit, or add an explicit edit control in the desktop part details. User, 2026-10-10: think about it more; a change must never alter the BOM of other projects by accident. KiCad facts found: placed symbols keep their own copy, including Exclude from BOM, in each schematic. A library change reaches a project only when someone runs Update Symbols from Library there, and Exclude from BOM changes only if that dialog option Update/reset symbol attributes is ticked. KiCad database libraries can map a 0/1 column to exclude_from_bom, exclude_from_board and exclude_from_sim. The desktop should show the setting either way.

title: Read more of KiCad's BOM markings and speed up binary blobs
description:
Low-priority follow-ups from the e4ee review:
- Old-format footprints with (attr virtual) are not treated as excluded from BOM. Check how KiCad treats them.
- A derived symbol (extends) does not take in_bom from its parent.
- The zero-loss report's Excluded from BOM check uses the same parser as the importer, so a parser bug would pass both.
- Blobs that are not UTF-8 still use the slow JavaScript SHA-256 (about 3 s per MiB). About 24 MiB of binary would hit the 60 s client timeout, though every real CAD file is UTF-8 today.

title: Smaller preview follow-ups: offline stored drawings, fallback notes, startup work
description:
From the c465/a133 review:
- F6: a cached stored drawing shows while the team server is down only within the same session, because the revisions the app knows about live in memory and are cleared at sign-in. Keep enough to find cached stored drawings after a restart.
- F8: if the local library also fails after a stored-bytes failure, the note is lost. A stored symbol that uses extends, or has no format_version, gets an error instead of a local drawing with a note.
- F9: the startup sweep and eviction run synchronously in Tauri setup, so the first start after a KiCad upgrade deletes the old version folder before the window appears. Move them to the background.
- The locked staging-folder code is copied in kicad-integration and tooling/catalog-import; move it to one shared place.

title: Share approved journey screenshots across machines
description: User decision, 2026-10-10: share them. The approved screenshots in apps/desktop/journeys/baselines/ depend on this machine: KiCad 10.0.4, installed fonts, the user name in temp paths (states 10-12, 20, 21) and the repo path (state 06). Blank out the machine-specific paths, and commit a small environment file (KiCad and WebView2 versions) so the runner says plainly when a machine differs, instead of reporting many pixel failures. CI is meant to run KiCad too (mx-f05667).

title: Clear the journey tooling's npm audit warning
description: From df4d. npm audit reports a high-severity issue in basic-ftp, pulled in through webdriverio 9; the fix is the breaking upgrade to webdriverio 10. It predates df4d. Also delete the old randomly named kicad-parts-* temp folders that earlier journey runs left in %TEMP%; new runs clean up after themselves.

title: Name the CSV catalog fixture in the glossary and retire 'oracle'
description: From the ff80 review. Comments and docs now say 'CSV catalog fixture', but the code still says 'oracle': about 55 uses in tooling/catalog-import/src/zero_loss.rs, the oracle() test helpers, and fields like oracle_import_problems and oracle_asset_path. The term also names both the tool and the recorded manifest. Ask the user whether to add a glossary entry, for example 'CSV catalog fixture: the recorded contents and hashes of the CSV catalog, used to prove nothing was changed or lost', with 'oracle' under Avoid; a plainer option is 'CSV catalog snapshot'. Then rename the oracle identifiers and update the old wording in mulch records mx-4c3a0d and mx-f8825d and in the plan pl-d0f7 prose. Optionally, give a plain error when an old manifest uses the 'diagnostics' key.

title: Roles, priority and change requests for catalog edits
description: User decisions, 2026-10-10. Replace the single Edit access setting (users.can_edit_catalog) with roles: Owner, Engineer, Purchaser, Viewer (glossary: docs/contexts/collaboration/CONTEXT.md). The Owner gives roles and priorities and can change anything. An Engineer changes part details and CAD items. A Purchaser changes supplier data and orders, but not part details. A Viewer changes nothing. The Owner gives each member a priority. When two members change the same field, the higher priority wins; with the same priority (for example, two engineers) the app asks which value to keep, as the 2254 conflict screen does today. Someone without enough access or priority is told so, and can send a change request instead. A change request waits in the inbox of every member with higher priority, who can accept or reject it, like a pull request. Still to settle while planning: what accepting a change request records. Follows kicad-parts-2254.

title: Read Excluded from BOM from KiCad's installed libraries
description: From the e4ee follow-up. The import sets Excluded from BOM only from our own symbol and footprint files. Footprints from KiCad's installed libraries are ignored, even though KiCad marks some of them, for example Connector:Tag-Connect_TC2030-IDC-FP_2x03_P1.27mm_Vertical has (attr exclude_from_pos_files exclude_from_bom). User decision, 2026-10-10: ART-0001-0006 (Tag-Connect TC2030) is a footprint only, with no part placed on the board (the cable is a tool), so it is Excluded from BOM. Read the flags from the user's KiCad install (same kicad-cli install as previews), record the KiCad version used, and make it an import problem when the install is missing.

title: Number CAD item revisions like parts
description: User decision on kicad-parts-9e05, 2026-10-10: option 1. Today a CAD item revision ID comes from its content (catalog_csv_imports.pb.js), so a footprint going A, B, then A again goes back to revision 1. Instead, number CAD item revisions like part revisions: going back to A adds revision 3, while the bytes stay stored once. The current revision is always the newest, which matches the glossary. KiCad check: KiCad database libraries point to symbols and footprints as Library:Name, with no revision, so KiCad always uses whatever the library file holds. KiCad Integration must therefore write each CAD item's current revision. Placed symbols keep their own copy in each schematic until someone runs Update Symbols from Library.

title: Let people accept CSV changes on edited parts, field by field
description: User decision, 2026-10-10. Edits made in the app always win over CSV imports. Today, when a CSV row changes for a part that was edited in the app, the import leaves the part alone and records an import problem (catalog_csv_imports.pb.js: the source row changed, but the current revision was not published by a CSV import). Show that import problem on the part in the desktop app. Opening it lists each field where the CSV differs from the current part details, with both values. The person picks which CSV values to accept; that saves a normal edit (a new revision with a reason) and resolves the import problem. Fields not picked stay as they are.

title: Add Masach Tech MS128-10F as a second manufacturer part of RFM-0000-0001
description: User decision, 2026-10-10. The g-rfm.csv MPN2 value MS128-10F is not a Wurth part: it is a Masach Tech two-piece RF shield frame, 12.8 x 12.3 x 7.5 mm, tin-plated steel, apparently the same size as Wurth 3670128. After the full catalog import, add it to RFM-0000-0001 as a second manufacturer part (Masach Tech, MS128-10F) with a reviewed edit, once someone checks its pad layout matches the footprint g-rfm:H_Wurth_WE-SHC-SEAMLESS-FRAME_3670128. title: Make a revision mean a CAD change, and archive instead of restore
description: User decisions, 2026-10-10 (glossary updated in docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md). Old products must keep the exact parts they were designed with, while new designs use the newest. (1) A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions a part uses. Only a change to CAD adds a part revision. CAD content that is the same under a newer CAD item number is not a change. (2) Part details (description, value, datasheet) and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and are shared by every revision. Changing them is recorded in the history (Change and audit entry, with who, when, why and before/after) but adds no revision. (3) A part that can no longer replace the old one (different package, pinout or value) gets a new IPN, not a revision. (4) Restore goes away. A bad revision is archived instead: hidden from KiCad and the app so nobody new picks it, still found by designs that use it, never deleted. The current revision is the newest revision that is not archived. (5) The IPN never carries the revision. Today every part details change adds a full revision (mx-88ce27) and the desktop has Restore (2254); both change here. Write a plan for the user to approve first: data model, migration of existing revisions, edit and conflict rules for shared details, import rules with the edits-win decision (kicad-parts-75a5), the desktop history, archive and roles (kicad-parts-5514).

title: Give KiCad one library entry per part revision
description: User decision, 2026-10-10. KiCad stores the name of each placed library entry in the design, and Update Symbols from Library and Update Footprints from Library fetch again by that name. So that an update never switches a design to a newer revision, KiCad gets one entry per part revision, with the revision in the name KiCad stores. The user confirmed the name format: the IPN followed by _v and the revision number, for example RES-0000-0470_v2; check it against KiCad naming rules, where a colon is never allowed. The same applies to symbol and footprint names for CAD item revisions, for example R_0603_v2. The IPN field and the BOM keep the plain IPN, with the revision in its own field. Show the current revision of each part in the main library, older revisions in a separate older-revisions library, and archived revisions nowhere. Moving a design to a newer revision is always a deliberate choice. Choose between a KiCad database library (.kicad_dbl, see the kicad-integration reference record) and generated library files. Depends on the revision remodel kicad-parts-bd76.
